method: Library-level: FileInfo::run on each input with the flags the oracle passed the tool (including source_dangling_references, which the tool sets under decision D10); text and TSV compared byte for byte with the retained Release C++ reports after replacing the 'File name: ' text line, the 'general: file name' TSV line and the failure line of -i, which all embed the input path. Tool-level: the exit codes of -i through run_with.
evidence: Tier 1 (executed differential): the Release C++ FileInfo of openms4-release-bc9cc12-c19e494-174b576, at all three pins this port follows, ran 59 cases on ibminode06 twice, reproduced (../oracle/a6-fileinfo/manifest.json). 38 of them have both reports compared here byte for byte, one (i_truncated_index) its text and one (i_window_below) its report against the padded file's, which is exactly native difference 11; the others carry exit codes, counts and refusals. Three masks: the "FileInfo took" stdout line; the ProgressLogger "-- done [took ...] --" lines, which carry wall and CPU seconds, and which only the case that reproduces TOPP_FileInfo_19 verbatim emits; and, for i_window_below alone, the bytes findIndexListOffset dumps to stderr after "Maybe this is not a indexedMzML.", which on a file shorter than its 1023-byte search window are an uninitialised heap buffer and differ from run to run (the manifest records both runs' raw hashes under indeterminate_stderr). None of the three goes into -out or -out_tsv, and the cases whose dump is the file's real tail are left unmasked and reproduce exactly. Tier 1 (retained upstream definition): TOPP_FileInfo_11 and _19 reproduced, including _11's WILL_FAIL exit code; _12's exit code and _6 are out of reach for reader reasons recorded below. Tier 4: the two places the source is undefined (an empty SRM chromatogram read with front()/back(), a NaN in one of the two std::sort calls) are refused, and the CorruptionInfo and DetailInfo aggregates the source declares and never fills stay at their defaults.

known_gaps.what: the -c duplicate-data-array-name line cannot be reached through the mzML reader
known_gaps.why: src/format/mzml.rs:1038 refuses a repeated auxiliary array name with Error::Parse("duplicate auxiliary array name"); the C++ reader loads such a file and leaves the report to -c. The oracle cases c_arrays and c_arrays_mixed record what the C++ writes; the port's rendering of the line is covered by a unit test of src/format/file_info/checks.rs on an experiment built in memory.
known_gaps.owner: the mzML reader (A3/P2), not this package

known_gaps.what: the -c MS-level-0 line is reachable only for an optical scan mode
known_gaps.why: src/kernel.rs:810-821 refuses a spectrum with ms_level 0 unless its scan mode is ElectromagneticRadiation, Emission or Absorption; the C++ loads an MS-level-0 mass spectrum. corrupt_scans.mzML gives its level-0 scan MS:1000806 "absorption spectrum" so both implementations load it and the line is exercised.
known_gaps.owner: the kernel spectrum invariant, not this package

known_gaps.what: TOPP_FileInfo_12's own input cannot be loaded
known_gaps.why: its "charge array" is stored as 64-bit float, which the strict mzML reader refuses ("canonical auxiliary array binary type"); A4 already records this. Its index is checked here and parses with the counts the C++ reports; the loadable cases use the core IndexedmzMLFile_1 fixture instead.
known_gaps.owner: the mzML reader (A3/P2), not this package

known_gaps.why: it runs -d on mzData, a peak format with no native reader on this path; the branch is refused with Error::Unsupported, as before this package.

known_gaps.what: the C++ decoder's stderr diagnostics are not written
known_gaps.why: IndexedMzMLDecoder prints "findIndexListOffset Error: ..." and a dump of the searched bytes on std::cerr (IndexedMzMLDecoder.cpp:198-200); this port writes nothing there. No report line depends on it, and the oracle case i_truncated_index shows the two agree on the report and the exit code.

known_gaps.what: a file shorter than 1023 bytes: the source reports no index where the port finds one
known_gaps.why: IndexedMzMLDecoder::findIndexListOffset seeks -1023 from the end and reads (IndexedMzMLDecoder.cpp:165-168); on a shorter file the seek fails, nothing is written into the buffer and the regex at :179-181 searches uninitialised memory, so the source's answer there is indeterminate and wave 5's rule does not ask for it. find_index_list_offset_with_buffer_size (src/format/indexed_mzml.rs:74) clamps the read to the file length and searches the whole file. Measured on the Release build: index_window_below.mzML (967 bytes, a valid index) reports no index and exits ILLEGAL_PARAMETERS, while index_window_above.mzML (the same file padded to 1217 bytes) parses; the port writes the padded file's report for both. Native difference 11.
known_gaps.owner: src/format/indexed_mzml.rs, which every index reader in the crate shares, not this package

known_gaps.what: an <index> whose first child is an <offset>, i.e. no whitespace immediately after the opening tag: the source drops that first offset, the port keeps it. Whitespace elsewhere inside <index> does not change it
known_gaps.why: domParseIndexedEnd_ walks the children as iter = getFirstChild(); while (iter != lastChild) { iter = getNextSibling(); ... } (IndexedMzMLDecoder.cpp:280-282 sets iter, :290-293 is the walk), advancing before it reads, so the first child is never looked at. A newline there makes it a text node and nothing is lost, which is why every index an OpenMS writer produces parses. Measured on the Release build: index_offsets_unspaced.mzML holds two spectrum offsets and the C++ counts one; the port counts two. Reproducing it would mean re-implementing the DOM walk in parse_offsets, which every other index reader calls. Native difference 12; the source defect is recorded for OpenMS_CPP_ISSUES.md.
